# E2E Test Coverage

<!-- Generated by frontend/scripts/generate-e2e-coverage.ts — do not edit by hand. -->

A complete inventory of the Playwright E2E suite: every project, every spec file, every test
title. All counts are derived from Playwright itself, so this file cannot drift out of sync
with the tests the way a hand-maintained list does.

Regenerate it after adding, renaming or removing tests:

```bash
just generate-e2e-coverage      # or: pnpm --prefix frontend generate-e2e-coverage
```

The generator shells out to `playwright test --list`, which only _collects_ tests — it starts
no web server and no browser, so it needs neither a running stack nor installed browsers.
`.github/workflows/lint-frontend.yml` regenerates this file on every PR and fails if the
committed copy differs.

There is one mode and one project list, so the inventory does not depend on a local
`frontend/.env` — see [README.md](./README.md).

## Gaps

Known gaps live in GitHub issues, not in this file — a hand-written "not covered" list goes
stale the moment someone writes the missing test. Open coverage issues:

- [#149](https://github.com/Blaxzter/wirksam/issues/149) — the date picker freezes the page on an arrow key. The
  keyboard test for it exists and is written correctly, but is marked `test.fixme()`
  (it wedges the renderer rather than failing an assertion). Remove the `fixme` when fixed.
- [#148](https://github.com/Blaxzter/wirksam/issues/148) — the light theme fails WCAG AA contrast via four theme
  tokens. `color-contrast` is the one axe rule the a11y suite defers; every other
  serious/critical rule is enforced at zero.

Not yet covered, and not currently tracked by an issue:

- User-management table pagination — needs enough seeded users to page. Listed in #136 but
  outside its acceptance criteria; the disposable-user fixture this would build on now exists.
- Demo data creation and deletion.

### Project `multi-user` — 4 files, 54 tests

#### `frontend/e2e/tests/multi-user/event-manager-access.spec.ts` — 24 tests

- **Event Manager – unpublished visibility** (5)
  - scoped manager can see unpublished event in list
  - scoped manager can open the event settings page for their event
  - scoped manager can see unpublished task in list
  - scoped manager can view unpublished task detail page
  - regular member cannot see unpublished event
- **Event Manager – task detail controls** (2)
  - scoped manager sees manage controls on managed task
  - scoped manager does NOT see manage controls on unmanaged task
- **Event Manager – edit page access** (2)
  - scoped manager can access edit page for managed task
  - event admin is bounced off the edit page of a task outside their events
- **Event Manager – CRUD operations** (8)
  - scoped manager can update task name
  - scoped manager can publish and unpublish task
  - scoped manager can delete task in managed event
  - scoped manager can create and delete a shift
  - scoped manager can update event name
  - scoped manager can publish event
  - event admin cannot delete the event, but the owner can
  - scoped manager can add shifts to task
- **Event Manager – cross-event isolation** (3)
  - scoped manager cannot update task in unmanaged event
  - event admin cannot read availabilities of an event they are not in
  - event admin cannot read the roster of an event they are not in
- **Event Manager – reporting** (2)
  - scoped manager can access reporting page
  - scoped manager sees reporting link in sidebar
- **Event Manager – self-service creation** (2)
  - a non-admin can create their own event and owns it
  - someone who runs an event sees My Events in the sidebar

- **Event members – People tab** (8)
